process_area.title: Event Marketing Strategy, Portfolio & Calendar Management

value_stream.name: Trade Show, Exhibition & Field Event Marketing

fields.Participants: CMO, Trade Sales (VS-11/VS-107), Trade-Pro Program (VS-43), Merchandising (VS-01), Insights (VS-44)
fields.Volume: Enterprise event-channel strategy (~40% B2B revenue base)

Controls: - CTL-647 (ensure controlled execution — Event Marketing Strategy, Portfolio & Calendar Management (PA-139.1).)
- CTL-647: event strategy approved by CMO; aligned to marketing/B2B strategy (VS-14)
Cross-references: - links to VS-14 (marketing), VS-44 (insights), VS-43 (trade-pro), VS-11/VS-107 (trade sales), W4194 (portfolio)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-strategy risk**: Events done ad-hoc, no portfolio logic; mitigated by documented channel strategy
- **Audience-mismatch risk**: Sponsoring events BuildRight's buyers don't attend; mitigated by audience-fit assessment
System Touchpoints: - Marketing strategy (VS-14); insights (VS-44); trade-pro base (VS-43); finance (VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Event Marketing define the role of events in the B2B/customer-acquisition mix (trade shows vs hosted trade days vs store events vs sponsorships), aligned to marketing strategy (VS-14) and B2B-growth goals

Event Marketing/Insights assess the event landscape (PhilConstruct, Worldbex, CebuCon, regional shows, association events) and audience fit vs BuildRight's trade/corporate segments (links to VS-44 insights, VS-43 trade-pro)
Event Marketing document the strategy, channel role, and investment envelope, obtain approval, and cascade to the annual portfolio/calendar (W4194)

fields.Participants: Marketing (VS-14), Trade Sales (VS-11/VS-107), Merchandising (VS-01), Store Ops (VS-07), Vendor Mgmt (VS-03)
fields.Volume: ~15–30 events/yr (national/regional shows + hosted events + store events)

Automation Opportunity: - Shared event-marketing calendar; portfolio-prioritization scoring; capacity-conflict alerts
Controls: - CTL-647 (ensure controlled execution — Event Marketing Strategy, Portfolio & Calendar Management (PA-139.1).)
- CTL-647: event calendar reconciled with promo/seasonal calendars; portfolio prioritized & approved
Cross-references: - links to VS-14 (marketing calendar), VS-01 §13.2 (seasonal), VS-58 (promo), VS-03 (vendor), VS-37 (grand opening), W4195 (budget), W4216 (ROI)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Calendar-conflict risk**: Events clash with promos/season/internal capacity; mitigated by integrated calendar
- **Over-commitment risk**: Too many events dilute focus/resources; mitigated by portfolio prioritization
System Touchpoints: - Event calendar/portfolio tool; marketing calendar (VS-14); seasonal (VS-01 §13.2); promo (VS-58); finance (VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Event Marketing build the annual event portfolio/calendar (priority trade shows, hosted trade days, product launches, store grand openings, sponsorships), sequenced with seasonal/merchandising calendar (VS-01 §13.2) and promo calendar (VS-58)
Event Marketing prioritize the portfolio by strategic fit, audience reach, lead/ROI potential, and budget (W4195), balancing national flagship vs regional/store events
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Finance / Trade Sales

steps.activity: Event Marketing publish the calendar, allocate owners/budget per event, and adjust quarterly based on performance (W4216) and opportunities

fields.Participants: Finance (VS-17.4/VS-34.3), Vendor Mgmt (VS-03/VS-39 co-op), Trade Sales, Procurement (VS-34)

workflows.name: Event Budget, Business Case & Sponsorship Funding

Automation Opportunity: - Event business-case templates; MDF/co-fund tracking; spend-vs-plan dashboards
Controls: - CTL-647 (ensure controlled execution — Event Marketing Strategy, Portfolio & Calendar Management (PA-139.1).)
- CTL-647: business case with ROI model approved; vendor MDF/co-op documented (VS-39); spend reconciled post-event
Cross-references: - links to VS-39.2 (co-op/MDF), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-34.3 (expense), VS-40 (capex), VS-34 (procurement), W4216 (ROI)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-ROI risk**: Events approved without a return model → unaccountable spend; mitigated by business case + post-event reconciliation
- **Funding-gap risk**: Over-reliance on own budget; mitigated by vendor MDF/co-op (VS-39)
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks per major event business case

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Finance build the event business case (booth/sponsorship cost, logistics, travel, samples, staff, MDF/co-fund links to VS-39) with target leads/sales and ROI model
Event Marketing/Vendor Mgmt secure vendor co-funding/co-exhibition (market-development funds, co-op links to VS-39.2), and structure sponsorship tiers/benefits with show organizers
Event Marketing/Finance route approval (capex/expense governance VS-40/VS-34.3), lock budget, and track spend vs plan post-event (W4216)

fields.Participants: Trade-Pro Program (VS-43), Key Accounts (VS-107), CDP (VS-126), Insights (VS-44)
fields.Volume: ~5,200 trade accounts + ~200 corporate accounts + prospects; show audiences ~10K–100K+

Automation Opportunity: - CDP-driven audience targeting; invitation/RSVP automation; account-mapping tools
Controls: - CTL-647 (ensure controlled execution — Event Marketing Strategy, Portfolio & Calendar Management (PA-139.1).)
- CTL-647: audience targeting data-privacy compliant (VS-91); consent for marketing captured
Cross-references: - links to VS-126 (CDP), VS-43 (trade-pro), VS-107 (key accounts), VS-14 (marketing automation), VS-91 (consent/privacy), W4214 (lead routing)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wrong-audience risk**: Inviting low-fit attendees; mitigated by audience targeting from CDP
- **Low-attendance risk**: Poor invitation execution; mitigated by multi-channel + account-manager outreach
System Touchpoints: - CDP/CRM (VS-126); trade-pro base (VS-43); email/marketing automation (VS-14); insights (VS-44)

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Trade Sales define the target audience per event (segments, geography, account tier — trade-pro, named accounts, prospects) from the CDP/trade-pro base (VS-126/VS-43)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Trade Sales / CDP

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Trade-Pro execute invitations/registration (email, call, account-manager outreach, VIP pass), and manage RSVP/attendance logistics
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Trade-Pro / Key Accounts

steps.activity: Event Marketing capture pre-event audience data (registrations, account mapping) for lead-routing (W4214) and measure attendance vs target (W4216)

fields.Owner: Event Marketing Manager / Vendor Mgmt (VS-03) / Trade Marketing
fields.Volume: ~800–1,000 vendors (esp. top-20 = 45% COGS, and branded suppliers)

Automation Opportunity: - MDF/co-fund tracking; vendor co-exhibition portal; contribution reconciliation
Controls: - CTL-647: vendor co-fund agreement with ABC compliance (VS-86.3); MDF reconciled (VS-39.2)
Cross-references: - links to VS-39.2 (co-op/MDF), VS-03 (vendor), VS-100.3 (legal/contracts), VS-86.3 (ABC), VS-17.4 (finance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unrecovered-funding risk**: Vendor MDF not claimed → BuildRight bears full cost; mitigated by MDF tracking (VS-39.2)
- **ABC risk**: Vendor 'sponsorship' masking inducements; mitigated by ABC controls (VS-86.3) and transparent agreements

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Vendor Mgmt identify co-funding/co-exhibition partners (brands wanting trade-show presence, product-launch tie-ins), and pitch co-exhibition/sponsorship/MDF (links to VS-39.2)
Event Marketing/Vendor Mgmt structure the co-fund agreement (scope, contribution, branding, lead-sharing, ABC compliance VS-86.3) and coordinate logistics (booth space, samples, demonstrators)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Vendor Mgmt / Legal

steps.activity: Event Marketing reconcile vendor contributions vs spend (links to VS-39.2 co-op settlement), manage partner relationships, and report co-fund ROI (W4216)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Finance / Vendor Mgmt

fields.Participants: Compliance (VS-22), Legal (VS-100.3), LGU Affairs (VS-76), Privacy (VS-91), DTI (VS-117)
fields.Trigger: Event with public presence, raffle/prize, LGU/exhibition permit need
fields.Volume: Per-event compliance (permits, prize-promo, ABC, data privacy)

Automation Opportunity: - Permit-calendar tracking; promo-permit checklist; consent-capture automation
Controls: - CTL-647: event/promo permits secured (VS-22.1/DTI); lead-data consent (VS-91); ABC for hospitality (VS-86.3); sample safety (VS-117/VS-114)
Cross-references: - links to VS-22.1 (permits), VS-76.1 (LGU), VS-58 (promo), VS-79 (prize tax), VS-91 (privacy), VS-86.3 (ABC), VS-117/VS-114 (product safety)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Permit-lapse risk**: Operating an event/promo without permit → fines/stop-order; mitigated by permit calendar
- **Prize/privacy/ABC risk**: Non-compliant raffle, lead-data misuse, or improper hospitality; mitigated by Legal/Privacy/ABC review
System Touchpoints: - Permits (VS-22.1); LGU (VS-76.1); promo (VS-58); tax/withholding (VS-79); privacy (VS-91); ABC (VS-86.3); product standards (VS-117/VS-114)
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks per event compliance (lead-time for permits)

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Compliance secure event permits (LGU/exhibition-organizer, DTI for promo permits, local permits for hosted events links to VS-22.1/VS-76.1) and meet organizer/exhibition rules
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Compliance / LGU Affairs

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Legal govern promo-prize mechanics (raffle/contest permits, DTI promo-permit, fairness, terms — links to VS-58 promo, VS-22.1), and ensure prize sourcing/tax (links to VS-79 withholding)

Event Marketing/Privacy ensure data-privacy compliance (lead-data consent, registration privacy notice links to VS-91), ABC for hospitality/gifts (VS-86.3), and product-safety/labeling for samples (VS-117/VS-114)

fields.Participants: Trade Sales (VS-11/VS-107), Merchandising (VS-01), Trade-Pro (VS-43), Store Ops (VS-07), HR (VS-19), Vendors
fields.Volume: Per-event team (sales, merchandising, marketing, trade specialists, store staff, vendors)

Automation Opportunity: - Event-team RACI templates; rostering tools; resource-checklist automation
Controls: - CTL-647 (ensure controlled execution — Event Marketing Strategy, Portfolio & Calendar Management (PA-139.1).)
- CTL-647: event team RACI defined; resource checklist verified pre-event
Cross-references: - links to VS-19.3 (rostering), VS-124 (sales enablement), VS-14 W1270 (print/collateral), VS-34 (procurement), VS-11/VS-107 (trade sales)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Staffing-gap risk**: Under/over-staffed booth; mitigated by roster planning
- **Resource-miss risk**: Samples/collateral/equipment missing at event; mitigated by resource checklist
System Touchpoints: - HR/rostering (VS-19.3); print/collateral (VS-14 W1270); procurement (VS-34); sales enablement (VS-124)

steps.activity: Event Marketing assemble the cross-functional event team (event lead, sales/booth staff, trade specialists, merchandising, store staff for hosted events), and define roles/RACI
Event Marketing/HR plan staffing/roster (booth shifts, travel, accommodation), and coordinate training (product knowledge, demo skills, lead-capture — links to VS-124)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / HR / Trade Specialists

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Procurement plan resources (booth/stand, collateral, samples, AV, travel, giveaways — links to VS-14 W1270 print, VS-34 procurement), and confirm logistics

Automation Opportunity: - Event-brief templates; SMART-metric library; lead-attribution CRM integration
Controls: - CTL-647 (ensure controlled execution — Event Marketing Strategy, Portfolio & Calendar Management (PA-139.1).)
- CTL-647: SMART success metrics defined pre-event; measurement method confirmed
Cross-references: - links to VS-14 (marketing), VS-11/VS-107 (sales/CRM), VS-44 (insights), VS-17.4 (ROI), W4214 (lead capture), W4216 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vague-objective risk**: "Brand awareness" with no metric → unmeasurable; mitigated by SMART metrics
- **Attribution-gap risk**: Can't tie event to pipeline; mitigated by lead-capture + CRM attribution (W4214/W4216)
System Touchpoints: - Event brief/metrics tool; CRM/lead pipeline (VS-11/VS-107); insights (VS-44); finance ROI (VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Event Marketing author the event brief (objective — leads/sales/brand/relationship; audience; key messages; product focus; offer), aligned to strategy (W4193)
Event Marketing/Trade Sales define SMART success metrics (leads, qualified-lead %, meetings, pipeline/sales attributed, cost-per-lead, NPS/brand-lift) and measurement method (W4216)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Trade Sales / Insights

steps.activity: Event Marketing brief the team (W4199) and vendors (W4197), confirm the lead-capture mechanism (W4214), and lock the success-metric baseline
